name: @mcp-abap-adt/compact

tools.name: HandlerGet
tools.description: [read-only] Reads one part of the object named by object_type and its name parameter (class_name, program_name, ddl_name, table_name, …). part selects it: source (default) the source alone, in one request; metadata the ADT metadata document alone, in one request; urls (SERVICE_BINDING) the service URL, its $metadata and the browser preview, contents (PACKAGE) the objects the package holds, its walk read level by level in ADT batch envelopes; package_names lists several packages, read together, one entry per package in the order given. A source document answers { part: 'source', source } and a metadata document { part: 'metadata', metadata }, beside the object's name. Parts per type: PACKAGE metadata, contents; DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, FUNCTION_GROUP metadata; LOCAL_TEST_CLASS, LOCAL_TYPES, LOCAL_DEFINITIONS, LOCAL_MACROS, TRANSPORT, UNIT_TEST, CDS_UNIT_TEST source; SERVICE_BINDING source, metadata, urls; every other type source, metadata. A part outside the type's list is answered with that list. Three parts read the repository by ADT address: object_structure(object_adt_type*, object_name*), node_structure(object_adt_type*, object_name*, node_id, with_short_descriptions; one node level; a package's blank answer is the empty listing with blank stating its two readings: an empty package, or an unknown package name) and virtual_folders(object_search_pattern, preselection, facet_order, with_versions, ignore_short_descriptions). Two parts read an activation run by its id, in one request each: activation_status(run_id*) answers { run_id, part, status, document }, the run's status (finished, error, failed, or its progress while it runs) and its status document as SAP answered it; activation_results(run_id*) answers { run_id, part, messages, document }, the messages the run produced and its results document as SAP answered it. Otherwise object_type required: PACKAGE(package_name*; part contents: package_name* or package_names*), DOMAIN(domain_name*), DATA_ELEMENT(data_element_name*), TABLE(table_name*), STRUCTURE(structure_name*), DDL(ddl_name*), SERVICE_DEFINITION(service_definition_name*), SERVICE_BINDING(service_binding_name*), CLASS(class_name*), LOCAL_TEST_CLASS(class_name*), LOCAL_TYPES(class_name*), LOCAL_DEFINITIONS(class_name*), LOCAL_MACROS(class_name*), PROGRAM(program_name*) [onprem only], INTERFACE(interface_name*), FUNCTION_GROUP(function_group_name*), FUNCTION_MODULE(function_module_name* as GROUP|MODULE, or function_module_name* with function_group_name*), BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION(behavior_definition_name*), BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION(behavior_implementation_name*), METADATA_EXTENSION(metadata_extension_name*), UNIT_TEST(run_id*), CDS_UNIT_TEST(run_id*), TRANSPORT(transport_number*). TRANSPORT answers the objects a task holds, each with its position in the task's object list; for a request, every task's entries, each once, with its task number and position. UNIT_TEST and CDS_UNIT_TEST read the run's result in one request and answer { success, run_id, run_result }, run_result the result document SAP answered, parsed. Valid once the status is FINISHED; a finished run's result carries executionTime. Runs on an ABAP session of its own. Optional timeout (seconds): when it passes, the read is cancelled, its ABAP session logged off, and the system stays as it was. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a client's cancel ends only the client's wait, and SAP runs the read on. When part is source (absent reads as source) and object_type is one of TRANSPORT, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING, CLASS, LOCAL_TEST_CLASS, LOCAL_TYPES, LOCAL_DEFINITIONS, LOCAL_MACROS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_MODULE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION; or part is metadata and object_type is one of PACKAGE, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, FUNCTION_GROUP, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING, CLASS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_MODULE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION; or part is object_structure; or part is node_structure and object_adt_type is given; or part is virtual_folders; or part is activation_status and run_id is given; or part is activation_results and run_id is given; or part is source (absent reads as source) and object_type is one of UNIT_TEST, CDS_UNIT_TEST and run_id is given, recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the answer: a whole number, at least 1, no default — without it the call waits until SAP answers. When it passes, the read is cancelled (its ABAP session is logged off) and the call answers that nothing was changed. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a cancel does nothing to SAP. Applies to the repository reads: object_type PACKAGE, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING, CLASS, LOCAL_TEST_CLASS, LOCAL_TYPES, LOCAL_DEFINITIONS, LOCAL_MACROS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION, TRANSPORT, and the parts object_structure, node_structure, virtual_folders.

object_type.description: ABAP object type for routed compact operation.

part.description: The part to read: source (the source alone), metadata (the ADT metadata document alone), urls (the service and preview URLs), contents (the objects a package holds); each object type answers the parts it has, and a part outside them is answered with the list of its parts. Three parts read the repository by ADT address: object_structure (object_adt_type*, object_name*), node_structure (object_adt_type*, object_name*, node_id, with_short_descriptions) and virtual_folders (object_search_pattern, preselection, facet_order, with_versions, ignore_short_descriptions). Two parts read an activation run by run_id*: activation_status (its status) and activation_results (the messages it produced).

package_names.description: Several package names (part contents), read together: one entry per package, in the order given, each { package_name, contents } or { package_name, error }.

max_results.description: Maximum number of members listed per package (part contents).

include_descriptions.description: Include each member's description (part contents). The walk's levels are then read as single requests, several at a time, rather than in ADT batch envelopes.

function_module_name.description: Function module name: GROUP|MODULE, its function group first, or the module alone with function_group_name.

function_group_name.description: Function group name (FUNCTION_GROUP; FUNCTION_MODULE given as the module's name).

transport_number.description: Transport request or task number (TRANSPORT). A request lists the entries of all its tasks; a task lists its own.

run_id.description: Run id: a unit test run (UNIT_TEST, CDS_UNIT_TEST) or an activation run (parts activation_status, activation_results).

object_adt_type.description: ADT type code of the object (object_structure) or of the parent node (node_structure).

node_id.description: Node id to expand (node_structure); the root when absent.

tools.name: HandlerSearch
tools.description: [read-only] Searches the ABAP repository for the objects whose name matches query, a name or a mask. Required: query*. Optional: object_type, max_results (default 100). Response: one object per line. Runs on an ABAP session of its own. Optional timeout (seconds): when it passes, the read is cancelled, its ABAP session logged off, and the system stays as it was. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a client's cancel ends only the client's wait, and SAP runs the read on. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the answer: a whole number, at least 1, no default — without it the call waits until SAP answers. When it passes, the read is cancelled (its ABAP session is logged off) and the call answers that nothing was changed. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a cancel does nothing to SAP.

query.description: Object name or mask, with * as a wildcard.

object_type.description: ADT object type to restrict the search to.

tools.name: HandlerWhereUsed
tools.description: [read-only] Lists where the object named by object_type and object_name is used — a class, interface, program, include, function group, function module (BAPI included), package, table, structure, domain, data element or CDS DDL source: the objects that use, call or reference it, with type and package. Required: object_type*, object_name*. Optional: function_group_name (FUNCTION_MODULE), max_results (default 100). Response: JSON. Runs on an ABAP session of its own. Optional timeout (seconds): when it passes, the read is cancelled, its ABAP session logged off, and the system stays as it was. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a client's cancel ends only the client's wait, and SAP runs the read on. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the answer: a whole number, at least 1, no default — without it the call waits until SAP answers. When it passes, the read is cancelled (its ABAP session is logged off) and the call answers that nothing was changed. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a cancel does nothing to SAP.

object_type.description: Type of the object whose usages are listed.

function_group_name.description: Function group of the function module (FUNCTION_MODULE).

max_results.description: Maximum number of referencing objects returned.

tools.name: HandlerGetData
tools.description: [read-only] Reads the rows of the table or CDS view named by object_name, or the rows sql_query selects: every column of object_name, or what sql_query selects with its columns, conditions and order. Required: object_name or sql_query. Optional: max_rows (default 100). Response: JSON. Runs on an ABAP session of its own. Optional timeout (seconds): when it passes, the read is cancelled, its ABAP session logged off, and the system stays as it was. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a client's cancel ends only the client's wait, and SAP runs the read on. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the answer: a whole number, at least 1, no default — without it the call waits until SAP answers. When it passes, the read is cancelled (its ABAP session is logged off) and the call answers that nothing was changed. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a cancel does nothing to SAP.

object_name.description: Table or CDS view whose rows are read, all columns. Used when sql_query is absent.

sql_query.description: ABAP SQL SELECT naming the columns, conditions and order to read.

tools.name: HandlerValidate
tools.description: [read-only] Validates a new object named by object_type and object_name before it is created. object_type required: CLASS(object_name*, superclass), PROGRAM(object_name*) [onprem only], INTERFACE(object_name*), FUNCTION_GROUP(object_name*), FUNCTION_MODULE(object_name* as GROUP|MODULE), TABLE(object_name*), STRUCTURE(object_name*), DDL(object_name*), DOMAIN(object_name*), DATA_ELEMENT(object_name*), PACKAGE(object_name*, super_package), BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION(object_name*), BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION(object_name*), METADATA_EXTENSION(object_name*), SERVICE_BINDING(object_name*=service_binding_name*, service_definition_name*). Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

object_type.description: Object type to validate before create. Supported: CLASS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, PACKAGE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION, SERVICE_BINDING.

object_name.description: Required object name. For SERVICE_BINDING this is the service binding name; a function module is named GROUP|MODULE.

package_name.description: Optional package context for validation (especially for create scenarios).

super_package.description: Super package of the package to validate (PACKAGE).

superclass.description: Superclass of the class to validate (CLASS).

description.description: Optional object description used during validation.

behavior_definition.description: Optional behavior definition name, used when validating behavior implementation.

root_entity.description: Optional CDS root entity name, used for behavior-related validation.

implementation_type.description: Optional implementation type, used for behavior implementation validation.

service_definition_name.description: Required when object_type=SERVICE_BINDING. Service definition paired with the binding.

service_binding_version.description: Optional service binding version for SERVICE_BINDING.

tools.name: HandlerCheckRun
tools.description: [read-only] Runs a syntax check on the object named by object_type and object_name. object_type required: CLASS(object_name*), PROGRAM(object_name*) [onprem only], INTERFACE(object_name*), FUNCTION_GROUP(object_name*), FUNCTION_MODULE(object_name* as GROUP|MODULE), TABLE(object_name*), STRUCTURE(object_name*), DDL(object_name*), DOMAIN(object_name*), DATA_ELEMENT(object_name*), PACKAGE(object_name*), BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION(object_name*), METADATA_EXTENSION(object_name*). source_code checks unsaved source given in the call, for CLASS, STRUCTURE and DDL. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

object_type.description: Object type. Supported: CLASS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, PACKAGE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, METADATA_EXTENSION.

object_name.description: Object name. A function module is named GROUP|MODULE, its function group first.

source_code.description: Source to check instead of the saved one; nothing is saved. CLASS, STRUCTURE and DDL only.

tools.name: HandlerDeletionCheck
tools.description: [read-only] Asks SAP whether the object named by object_type and object_name can be deleted: sends the deletion check request for its type, and answers SAP's verdict as it came: deletable true with the object and SAP's message when it carries one, or SAP's refusal with its words. object_type and object_name required: PACKAGE, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING, CLASS, CDS_UNIT_TEST (its test class), PROGRAM [onprem only], INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE (object_name GROUP|MODULE), BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

object_type.description: Object type. Supported: PACKAGE, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING, CLASS, CDS_UNIT_TEST, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION.

object_name.description: Object name. A function module is named GROUP|MODULE, its function group first.

tools.name: HandlerUnitTestStatus
tools.description: [read-only] Reads the status of the ABAP Unit test run named by run_id. Required: run_id*. Optional: with_long_polling. Response: JSON. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

with_long_polling.description: Use long polling while waiting for completion.

tools.name: HandlerUnitTestResult
tools.description: [read-only] Reads the result of the ABAP Unit test run named by run_id*, in one request (GET /sap/bc/adt/abapunit/results/{run_id}), and answers { success, run_id, run_result }: run_result is the result document SAP answered, parsed. Valid once the status is FINISHED; a finished run's result carries executionTime. Optional: with_navigation_uris, format (abapunit or junit). When run_id is given, recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

with_navigation_uris.description: Include ADT navigation URIs in the result payload.

tools.name: HandlerCdsUnitTestStatus
tools.description: [read-only] Reads the status of the CDS unit test run named by run_id. Required: run_id*. Optional: with_long_polling. Response: JSON. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

with_long_polling.description: Use long polling while waiting for completion.

tools.name: HandlerCdsUnitTestResult
tools.description: [read-only] Reads the result of the CDS unit test run named by run_id*, in one request (GET /sap/bc/adt/abapunit/results/{run_id}), and answers { success, run_id, run_result }: run_result is the result document SAP answered, parsed. Valid once the status is FINISHED; a finished run's result carries executionTime. Optional: with_navigation_uris, format (abapunit or junit). When run_id is given, recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

with_navigation_uris.description: Include ADT navigation URIs in the result payload.

tools.name: HandlerProfileList
tools.description: [read-only] Lists the ABAP profiler trace files. Response: JSON. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

tools.name: HandlerProfileView
tools.description: [read-only] Reads the ABAP profiler trace named by trace_id_or_uri in the view given (hit list, statements or database accesses), raw or analysed. Required: trace_id_or_uri*, view*(hitlist|statements|db_accesses). Optional: mode(raw|analyze, default raw), top(analyze only), with_system_events, id, with_details, auto_drill_down_threshold. Response: JSON. Runs on an ABAP session of its own. Optional timeout (seconds): when it passes, the read is cancelled, its ABAP session logged off, and the system stays as it was. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a client's cancel ends only the client's wait, and SAP runs the read on. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the answer: a whole number, at least 1, no default — without it the call waits until SAP answers. When it passes, the read is cancelled (its ABAP session is logged off) and the call answers that nothing was changed. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a cancel does nothing to SAP.

mode.description: "raw" returns the parsed trace payload as-is (default). "analyze" returns a compact summary instead — totals plus the top-ranked entries — via the same trace view.

top.description: Number of top-ranked rows to include when mode is "analyze". Default 10. Ignored for mode "raw".

tools.name: HandlerDumpList
tools.description: [read-only] Reads one page of the runtime feed named by feed_type in one request, newest first: the ABAP short dumps (runtime errors) of the user, object_name or time range from–to given, or system messages or SAP Gateway errors. Optional: feed_type(dumps|system_messages|gateway_errors, default dumps), user, runtime_error, exception, object_name, package, component, top (1 to 100), from, to. Response: JSON { feed_type, count, entries, next_to }; each dump carries dump_id; next_to is the `to` of SAP's next link, present when more remain. The next link's page starts at the boundary second, inclusive: entries of that second may repeat; match them by dump_id. Runs on an ABAP session of its own. Optional timeout (seconds): when it passes, the read is cancelled, its ABAP session logged off, and the system stays as it was. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a client's cancel ends only the client's wait, and SAP runs the read on. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the answer: a whole number, at least 1, no default — without it the call waits until SAP answers. When it passes, the read is cancelled (its ABAP session is logged off) and the call answers that nothing was changed. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a cancel does nothing to SAP.

feed_type.description: Which runtime feed to list. Default "dumps" (ABAP short dumps). "system_messages" and "gateway_errors" read the other two ADT runtime feeds through the same call.

runtime_error.description: Dumps whose runtime error contains this text, in any case.

exception.description: Dumps whose exception class contains this text, in any case.

object_name.description: Dumps whose terminated object name contains this text, in any case.

package.description: Dumps whose object package contains this text, in any case.

component.description: Dumps whose application component contains this text, in any case.

top.description: Entries the page holds, 1 to 100 (SAP answers 100 when top is absent).

to.description: End of time range (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS), inclusive: the page holds the entries up to that second; a previous answer's next_to is the next page's to, and that page starts at the boundary second, inclusive.

tools.name: HandlerDumpView
tools.description: [read-only] Reads the ABAP short dump (runtime error) named by dump_id in the view given. Required: dump_id* (id or URI). Optional: view(default|summary|formatted). Response: JSON. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

dump_id.description: The dump's dump_id, or its URI.

view.description: "summary" — runtime error, exception, terminated program, time, user and termination position; "default" — that summary and the parsed dump; "formatted" — the dump as formatted text.

tools.name: HandlerServiceBindingListTypes
tools.description: [read-only] Lists the available service binding types. Optional: response_format(xml|json|plain). Response: XML/JSON/plain by response_format. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

response_format.description: Response format for protocol types list.

tools.name: HandlerServiceBindingValidate
tools.description: [read-only] Validates a new service binding named by service_binding_name for the service definition named by service_definition_name, before it is created. Required: service_binding_name*, service_definition_name*. Optional: service_binding_version, package_name, description. Response: JSON. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

service_definition_name.description: Service definition name to pair with binding.

tools.name: HandlerCreate
tools.description: Creates the object named by object_type and its name parameter (class_name, program_name, ddl_name, table_name, …): sends the create request for its type with the given parameters, and answers SAP's result. The object is created inactive. object_type required: PACKAGE(package_name*, super_package*), DOMAIN(domain_name*, package_name*), DATA_ELEMENT(data_element_name*, package_name*), TRANSPORT(description*), TABLE(table_name*, package_name*), STRUCTURE(structure_name*, package_name*), DDL(ddl_name*, package_name*), SERVICE_DEFINITION(service_definition_name*, package_name*), SERVICE_BINDING(service_binding_name*, service_definition_name*, package_name*), CLASS(class_name*, package_name*), PROGRAM(program_name*, package_name*) [onprem only], INTERFACE(interface_name*, package_name*), FUNCTION_GROUP(function_group_name*, package_name*), FUNCTION_MODULE(function_module_name*, function_group_name*), BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION(name*, package_name*, implementation_type*), BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION(class_name*, package_name*), METADATA_EXTENSION(name*, package_name*). Optional for every type: description, transport_request. When object_type is one of DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, TRANSPORT, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING, CLASS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION; or object_type is PACKAGE and the connection is HTTP, recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

object_type.description: ABAP object type for routed compact operation.

function_group_name.description: ABAP function group name (FUNCTION_GROUP; the group of a FUNCTION_MODULE).

ddl_name.description: DDL source name (CDS view, AMDP table function, etc.).

transport_request.description: Transport request id (if required by system).

master_language.description: Original language of the created object; the session language when absent.

target_system.description: Target system of the transport request (TRANSPORT create).

owner.description: Owner of the transport request (TRANSPORT create).

service_definition_name.description: Service definition name (SERVICE_DEFINITION; the definition a SERVICE_BINDING binds).

service_name.description: Service name of the binding (SERVICE_BINDING create); the binding name when absent.

service_version.description: Service version of the binding (SERVICE_BINDING create); 0001 when absent.

binding_variant.description: Binding variant (SERVICE_BINDING create); ODATA_V4_UI when absent.

name.description: Object name for handlers that require a generic `name` (behavior definition, metadata extension).

tools.name: HandlerUpdate
tools.description: Writes the object named by object_type and its name parameter (class_name, program_name, ddl_name, table_name, …) under its lock: sends the one write request of its type under lock_handle, the lock handle of the object, and answers SAP's result. The write sets the whole content to the one given. lock_handle and object_type required: PACKAGE(package_name*, source_code*, transport_request), DOMAIN(domain_name*, source_code*, transport_request), DATA_ELEMENT(data_element_name*, source_code*, transport_request), FUNCTION_GROUP(function_group_name*, source_code*, transport_request), TABLE(table_name*, ddl_code*, transport_request), STRUCTURE(structure_name*, ddl_code*, transport_request), DDL(ddl_name*, ddl_source*, transport_request), SERVICE_DEFINITION(service_definition_name*, source_code*, transport_request), CLASS(class_name*, source_code*, transport_request), LOCAL_TEST_CLASS(class_name*, test_class_code*, transport_request), LOCAL_TYPES(class_name*, local_types_code*, transport_request), LOCAL_DEFINITIONS(class_name*, definitions_code*, transport_request), LOCAL_MACROS(class_name*, macros_code*, transport_request), UNIT_TEST(class_name*, test_class_source*, transport_request), CDS_UNIT_TEST(class_name*, test_class_source*, transport_request), PROGRAM(program_name*, source_code*, transport_request) [onprem only], INTERFACE(interface_name*, source_code*, transport_request), FUNCTION_MODULE(function_module_name*, function_group_name*, source_code*, transport_request), BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION(name*, source_code*, transport_request), BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION(class_name*, implementation_code*, transport_request), METADATA_EXTENSION(name*, source_code*, transport_request), SERVICE_BINDING(service_binding_name*, desired_publication_state*, binding_variant*, service_name, service_version). For PACKAGE, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT and FUNCTION_GROUP, source_code is the whole metadata document, sent as given. For LOCAL_TEST_CLASS, LOCAL_TYPES, LOCAL_DEFINITIONS, LOCAL_MACROS, UNIT_TEST, CDS_UNIT_TEST and BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, lock_handle is the class's lock handle. For SERVICE_BINDING the write is its publication request, sent under the lock_handle given, an empty one included; service_name and service_version (default 0001) name the service of an OData V2 binding. transport_request is sent as the write's corrNr. Over Streamable HTTP the write takes the lock's state_handle: send it as the state_handle argument of every call under the lock (or in the x-mcp-state-handle header); the write is sent only under a lock the instance it reaches holds. When lock_handle is given and object_type is one of DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, FUNCTION_GROUP, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING, CLASS, LOCAL_TEST_CLASS, LOCAL_TYPES, LOCAL_DEFINITIONS, LOCAL_MACROS, UNIT_TEST, CDS_UNIT_TEST, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_MODULE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION; or lock_handle is given and object_type is PACKAGE and the connection is HTTP, recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

object_type.description: ABAP object type for routed compact operation.

lock_handle.description: The lock handle of the object (for a class include, of the class): the write is sent under it.

transport_request.description: Transport request id, sent as the write's corrNr (the types whose description names it).

tools.name: HandlerDelete
tools.description: Deletes the object named by object_type and its name parameter (class_name, program_name, ddl_name, table_name, …): sends the deletion request for its type, and answers SAP's result. object_type required: PACKAGE(package_name*, transport_request), DOMAIN(domain_name*, transport_request), DATA_ELEMENT(data_element_name*, transport_request), TABLE(table_name*, transport_request), STRUCTURE(structure_name*, transport_request), DDL(ddl_name*, transport_request), SERVICE_DEFINITION(service_definition_name*, transport_request), SERVICE_BINDING(service_binding_name*, transport_request), CLASS(class_name*, transport_request), CDS_UNIT_TEST(class_name*, transport_request), PROGRAM(program_name*, transport_request) [onprem only], INTERFACE(interface_name*, transport_request), FUNCTION_GROUP(function_group_name*, transport_request), FUNCTION_MODULE(function_module_name*, function_group_name*, transport_request), BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION(behavior_definition_name*, transport_request), BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION(behavior_implementation_name*, transport_request), METADATA_EXTENSION(metadata_extension_name*, transport_request), LOCAL_TEST_CLASS(class_name*, lock_handle*, transport_request), LOCAL_TYPES(class_name*, lock_handle*, transport_request), LOCAL_DEFINITIONS(class_name*, lock_handle*, transport_request), LOCAL_MACROS(class_name*, lock_handle*, transport_request), UNIT_TEST(class_name*, lock_handle*, transport_request). CDS_UNIT_TEST deletes its test class. For LOCAL_TEST_CLASS, LOCAL_TYPES, LOCAL_DEFINITIONS and LOCAL_MACROS (the class's local includes) and UNIT_TEST (its test classes include) the include is written empty under lock_handle, the class's lock handle. transport_request is sent with the request. Over Streamable HTTP an include write takes the lock's state_handle: send it as the state_handle argument of every call under the lock (or in the x-mcp-state-handle header); it is sent only under a lock the instance it reaches holds. When object_type is one of PACKAGE, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING, CLASS, CDS_UNIT_TEST, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION; or lock_handle is given and object_type is one of LOCAL_TEST_CLASS, LOCAL_TYPES, LOCAL_DEFINITIONS, LOCAL_MACROS, UNIT_TEST, recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

object_type.description: Object type. Supported: PACKAGE, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING, CLASS, CDS_UNIT_TEST, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION, LOCAL_TEST_CLASS, LOCAL_TYPES, LOCAL_DEFINITIONS, LOCAL_MACROS, UNIT_TEST.

lock_handle.description: The lock handle of the class (LOCAL_TEST_CLASS, LOCAL_TYPES, LOCAL_DEFINITIONS, LOCAL_MACROS, UNIT_TEST): the include is written empty under it.

ddl_name.description: DDL source name (CDS view, AMDP table function, etc.).

transport_request.description: Transport request id, sent with the deletion (or the include write).

tools.name: HandlerActivate
tools.description: Activates the object named by object_name and object_type (or object_adt_type), or the objects named by objects, in one request. Single form (object_name*, object_type or object_adt_type*): object_type is enough for CLASS, PROGRAM [onprem only], INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, METADATA_EXTENSION, PACKAGE, SERVICE_DEFINITION and SERVICE_BINDING; any other type takes object_adt_type (e.g. "CLAS/OC"). List form (objects[].name*, objects[].type*, objects[].parentName, objects[].uri); a function module is listed with objects[].parentName set to its function group, type FUGR/FF. One object of CLASS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION or METADATA_EXTENSION (by object_type or its ADT type code) is activated directly and answers the activation verdict. Every other call starts an activation run and answers { run_id }: the id of the accepted run, whose status and messages are read by that id. When objects is absent and object_adt_type is absent and object_type is one of DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, CLASS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, METADATA_EXTENSION; or objects is given; or objects is absent and object_adt_type is given; or objects is absent and object_adt_type is absent and object_type is one of PACKAGE, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING, recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

object_type.description: ABAP object type for routed compact operation. Names the object's type in the single form.

object_adt_type.description: ADT object type code (e.g. CLAS/OC, PROG/P) of the object (single form).

parentName.description: Owning object, for a part of one: a function module's function group.

tools.name: HandlerTransportCreate
tools.description: Transport create. Required: description*. Optional: transport_type(workbench|customizing), target_system, owner. Response: JSON. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

tools.name: HandlerTransportSortAndCompress
tools.description: Sorts the object list of the transport task named by transport_number and merges its duplicate entries. Required: transport_number* (a task). A task holding the same entry twice refuses removing an entry until this has run. Response: JSON — acceptance only; a re-read of the task's objects (object_type TRANSPORT) confirms it. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

transport_number.description: Number of the transport task to sort and compress.

tools.name: HandlerTransportMoveObjects
tools.description: Moves the object entries named by objects from the transport task named by transport_number to the task named by target_number. Required: transport_number* (the source task), target_number* (the target task), objects* (at least one: object_name*, object_type*, position* in the source task's object list, pgmid). The positions come from a read of the source task's objects (object_type TRANSPORT). Response: JSON — acceptance only; a re-read of both tasks' objects (object_type TRANSPORT) confirms it. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

transport_number.description: Number of the transport task that holds the entries.

target_number.description: Number of the transport task the entries move to.

object_type.description: Object-directory type — CLAS, FUGR, TABL, DOMA — not an ADT type code like CLAS/OC.

position.description: Position of the object's entry in the source task's object list.

pgmid.description: Program id. Defaults to R3TR, a workbench object's.

objects.description: The entries to move, at least one — each with object_name, object_type, position (in the source task) and an optional pgmid.

tools.name: HandlerLock
tools.description: Lock operation. object_type required: CLASS(object_name*), PROGRAM(object_name*) [onprem only], INTERFACE(object_name*), FUNCTION_GROUP(object_name*), FUNCTION_MODULE(object_name*), TABLE(object_name*), STRUCTURE(object_name*), DDL(object_name*), DOMAIN(object_name*), DATA_ELEMENT(object_name*), PACKAGE(object_name*), BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION(object_name*), BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION(object_name*), METADATA_EXTENSION(object_name*), SERVICE_DEFINITION(object_name*), SERVICE_BINDING(object_name*). When object_type is one of CLASS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING; or object_type is PACKAGE and the connection is HTTP, recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

object_type.description: Object type. Supported: CLASS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, PACKAGE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING.

tools.name: HandlerUnlock
tools.description: Unlock operation. object_type required: CLASS(object_name*, lock_handle*), PROGRAM(object_name*, lock_handle*) [onprem only], INTERFACE(object_name*, lock_handle*), FUNCTION_GROUP(object_name*, lock_handle*), FUNCTION_MODULE(object_name*, lock_handle*), TABLE(object_name*, lock_handle*), STRUCTURE(object_name*, lock_handle*), DDL(object_name*, lock_handle*), DOMAIN(object_name*, lock_handle*), DATA_ELEMENT(object_name*, lock_handle*), PACKAGE(object_name*, lock_handle*), BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION(object_name*, lock_handle*), BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION(object_name*, lock_handle*), METADATA_EXTENSION(object_name*, lock_handle*), SERVICE_DEFINITION(object_name*, lock_handle*), SERVICE_BINDING(object_name*, lock_handle*); an empty lock_handle of a SERVICE_BINDING answers that the binding is already unlocked. Over Streamable HTTP the unlock takes the lock's state_handle: send it as the state_handle argument of every call under the lock (or in the x-mcp-state-handle header); the unlock ends the instance's hold on the lock. When object_type is one of CLASS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING; or object_type is PACKAGE and the connection is HTTP, recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

object_type.description: Object type. Supported: CLASS, PROGRAM, INTERFACE, FUNCTION_GROUP, FUNCTION_MODULE, TABLE, STRUCTURE, DDL, DOMAIN, DATA_ELEMENT, PACKAGE, BEHAVIOR_DEFINITION, BEHAVIOR_IMPLEMENTATION, METADATA_EXTENSION, SERVICE_DEFINITION, SERVICE_BINDING.

tools.name: HandlerUnitTestRun

When runner is sync; or runner is async (absent reads as async), recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

tests.description: List of test classes to run.

runner.description: async (default): starts the run and returns its run_id, whose status and result are read by run_id; suited to long suites. sync: one request that runs every test class of each container_class and returns the finished result.

add_foreign_tests_as_preview.description: Preview foreign tests without full inclusion.

tools.name: HandlerProfileSchedule
tools.description: [read-only] Schedules an ABAP profiler trace in one request. Optional: description, profiling flags (all_procedural_units, all_misc_abap_statements, all_internal_table_events, all_dynpro_events, aggregate, explicit_on_off, with_rfc_tracing, all_system_kernel_events, sql_trace, all_db_events, max_size_for_trace_file, amdp_trace, max_time_for_tracing). tools.name: HandlerProfileRun
tools.description: [read-only] Runs a class or a program in one request. Required: target_type*(CLASS|PROGRAM) + class_name* for CLASS or program_name* for PROGRAM [onprem only — programs exist on premise]. Optional: profiler_id (the profiler id of a scheduled trace; given, the run goes under that trace; absent, the run is plain), background. Response: JSON { success, class_name | program_name, output }, plus profile: { profiler_id } for a run under a trace. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

profiler_id.description: The profiler id of a scheduled trace. Given, the run goes under that trace; absent, the run is plain.

background.description: When true, the run goes on in the background on an ABAP session of its own and the call answers at once with a run_handle; read its answer later with HandlerBackgroundRunGet, and remove it with HandlerBackgroundRunDiscard. A started run cannot be stopped. No default: without it the call waits for the run to end.

tools.name: HandlerDebugBreakpoints
tools.description: [read-only] Debugger breakpoints and watchpoints: each call sends one SAP request, the operation's, and answers what SAP answered. kind abap: setBreakpoints sets the breakpoint set of this debugging identity to breakpoints and answers each row SAP placed or refused; syncBreakpoints rewrites the full set (sync_scope full) or the part of the objects in sync_objects (sync_scope partial); deleteBreakpoint deletes breakpoint_id; createWatchpoint, listWatchpoints and deleteWatchpoint work on the attached debuggee. In user mode the breakpoints catch every request of the request user; the set is one per SAP user and request user, shared by every IDE of that user, and each change rewrites it as a whole. kind amdp: syncBreakpoints rewrites the breakpoints of the running AMDP session and answers the request id; SAP confirms them in a SYNC_BREAKPOINTS event. The answer carries state_handle, and for abap the identity in force. Runs outside batch mode.

state_handle.description: The handle of this server's debug state. abap setBreakpoints and syncBreakpoints open the debug state when it is omitted and answer its handle; every other operation takes it.

kind.description: abap works with the ABAP debugger; amdp with the AMDP debugger of SQLScript methods.

operation.description: The one request: abap setBreakpoints, syncBreakpoints, deleteBreakpoint, createWatchpoint, listWatchpoints or deleteWatchpoint; amdp syncBreakpoints.

breakpoints.description: setBreakpoints and syncBreakpoints: abap a line, an exception class, an ABAP statement or a message, a line breakpoint may carry a condition; amdp object_name (the class) and line of each, an empty list clears them.

object_type.description: For a line: CLAS, PROG, INCL or FUNC.

object_name.description: For a line: the object holding it.

line.description: For a line: the line in the object source.

include.description: For a class: definitions, implementations, macros or testclasses; the main source when omitted.

parent_name.description: For a function module: its function group.

exception_class.description: Stops where an exception of this class is raised.

statement.description: Stops at every ABAP statement of this keyword.

message.description: Stops where this message is sent: message class, number, type.

condition.description: A line breakpoint only: stops only when this ABAP condition holds.

sync_scope.description: abap syncBreakpoints: full replaces every breakpoint of the set; partial replaces those of the objects in sync_objects and takes line breakpoints.

sync_objects.description: abap syncBreakpoints with sync_scope partial: the ADT URIs of the objects whose breakpoints are replaced.

breakpoint_id.description: abap deleteBreakpoint: the id SAP gave the breakpoint.

condition.description: abap createWatchpoint: the ABAP condition the watchpoint stops on.

watchpoint_id.description: abap deleteWatchpoint: the id SAP gave the watchpoint.

request_user.description: abap, user mode: the SAP user whose requests the breakpoints and the listener catch; the connected SAP user when omitted. The first abap call of a debug state fixes it.

debugging_mode.description: abap: user (when omitted) catches every request of the request user; terminal catches the requests that carry this debug state's terminal_id and ide_id. The first abap call of a debug state fixes it.

detail.description: How much of the answer to return: "terse" (default, the fields you need to act), "full" (the whole parse), "raw" (the document as ADT sent it).

tools.name: HandlerDebugSession
tools.description: [read-only] Debugger listener and session. Each operation up to end sends one SAP request, the operation's, and answers what SAP answered. kind abap: checkListener answers whether another debugger holds this identity's debugging (SAP's 409 names the holder); listen waits for a debuggee for exactly hold_seconds, SAP's hold, and answers the debuggee caught (debuggee_id, its server) or caught: false; a breakpoint stops a program while a listen is open; stopListener ends the listener and deletes the identity's breakpoints; attach attaches debuggee_id on the attaching session, which the first attach opens and every later attach, step and reading uses; detachDebugger sends detachDebugger on the attaching session, which releases the debuggee, and the program runs on; terminateDebuggee ends the debuggee where it stands and terminateDebugger frees the debugger; each answers SAP's answer as it came, which is a 500 when it succeeded, and the next answer shows the success (noSessionAttached, or the program's end); setDebuggerSettings sends the settings given at the attached debuggee. kind amdp: start opens an AMDP session for the connected SAP user and answers its main_id; getEvents answers the events SAP sends (breaks with their debuggee ids, breakpoint confirmations, ends); stop ends the AMDP session; deleteDebuggee cancels the execution of debuggee_id. end, for either kind, takes state_handle and logs off each connection the debug state opened, one logoff each: an attached debuggee runs on, an AMDP debug session ends, and the user's breakpoints stay set until stopListener removes them; the debug state and its handle end with it, and a new debug state of either kind and any identity opens after it. The answer carries state_handle while the debug state holds something, and for abap the identity in force. Runs outside batch mode.

state_handle.description: The handle of this server's debug state. abap checkListener, listen, stopListener and attach, and amdp start, open the debug state when it is omitted and answer its handle; every other operation takes it.

kind.description: abap works with the ABAP debugger; amdp with the AMDP debugger of SQLScript methods.

operation.description: The one request: abap checkListener, listen, stopListener, attach, detachDebugger, terminateDebuggee, terminateDebugger or setDebuggerSettings; amdp start, getEvents, stop or deleteDebuggee. end, for either kind, logs off the debug state.

hold_seconds.description: abap listen: how long SAP holds the listen, in seconds; SAP answers at a catch or when the hold ends.

take_over.description: abap listen: true displaces another debugger listening for the same user; false, or omitted, answers its 409. amdp start: true ends an AMDP session of this user left behind.

debuggee_id.description: abap attach: the debuggee_id listen answered. amdp deleteDebuggee: the debuggee id of a break event.

server.description: abap attach: the debuggee's application server, as listen answered it.

settings.description: abap setDebuggerSettings: the settings sent; a field left out keeps its value.

system_debugging.description: Steps into system programs and stops at breakpoints there.

create_exception_object.description: Creates the exception object even where a CATCH does not ask for it.

request_user.description: abap, user mode: the SAP user whose requests the breakpoints and the listener catch; the connected SAP user when omitted. The first abap call of a debug state fixes it.

debugging_mode.description: abap: user (when omitted) catches every request of the request user; terminal catches the requests that carry this debug state's terminal_id and ide_id. The first abap call of a debug state fixes it.

detail.description: How much of the answer to return: "terse" (default, the fields you need to act), "full" (the whole parse), "raw" (the document as ADT sent it).

tools.name: HandlerDebugStep
tools.description: [read-only] Moves the stopped debuggee: each call sends one SAP request, the operation's. kind abap, on the attached debuggee: stepInto, stepOver, stepReturn and stepContinue step from where it stands; stepRunToLine runs to the line object_type, object_name and line name, stepJumpToLine moves there and skips what lies between; a step answers SAP's step result, or ended when SAP reports the program's end, and the stopped position is read from the stack. setStackPosition makes frame position the one variables are read in. kind amdp: stepOver and stepContinue move debuggee_id and answer the request id; the next stop arrives as a break event. Runs outside batch mode.

state_handle.description: Opaque handle identifying the server-held state this operation works on.

kind.description: abap works with the ABAP debugger; amdp with the AMDP debugger of SQLScript methods.

operation.description: The one request: abap stepInto, stepOver, stepReturn, stepContinue, stepRunToLine, stepJumpToLine or setStackPosition; amdp stepOver or stepContinue.

object_type.description: For a line: CLAS, PROG, INCL or FUNC.

object_name.description: For a line: the object holding it.

line.description: For a line: the line in the object source.

include.description: For a class: definitions, implementations, macros or testclasses; the main source when omitted.

parent_name.description: For a function module: its function group.

position.description: abap setStackPosition: the frame's position in the stack.

debuggee_id.description: amdp: the debuggee id of the break event.

detail.description: How much of the answer to return: "terse" (default, the fields you need to act), "full" (the whole parse), "raw" (the document as ADT sent it).

tools.name: HandlerDebugMaintain
tools.description: [read-only] Reads and changes the stopped debuggee: each call sends one SAP request, chosen by operation. kind abap, on the attached debuggee: getStack answers the frames, each with its program, include, line and ADT address, the stopped position on top; getVariables answers the variables in names (a path reads a component or a table row); getChildVariables answers the members of the ids in parents, the scopes (@ROOT) when parents is omitted; getMemorySizes answers the memory sizes; createMemorySnapshot creates a memory snapshot; setVariableValue sets variable_name to value and answers the variable. kind amdp: getDataPreview answers the rows of the table variable variable_name of debuggee_id. Runs outside batch mode.

state_handle.description: Opaque handle identifying the server-held state this operation works on.

kind.description: abap works with the ABAP debugger; amdp with the AMDP debugger of SQLScript methods.

operation.description: What the call does: abap getStack (the stack), getVariables (variables by name), getChildVariables (child variables), getMemorySizes (memory sizes), createMemorySnapshot (a snapshot) or setVariableValue (set a value); amdp getDataPreview (the data preview of a table variable).

parents.description: abap getChildVariables: the ids whose members are read; @ROOT, the scopes, when omitted.

variable_name.description: abap setVariableValue: the variable set. amdp getDataPreview: the table variable read.

debuggee_id.description: amdp getDataPreview: the debuggee id of the break event.

query.description: amdp getDataPreview: a SELECT over the table variable; every column when omitted.

row_number.description: amdp getDataPreview: how many rows SAP answers; SAP's own count when omitted.

detail.description: How much of the answer to return: "terse" (default, the fields you need to act), "full" (the whole parse), "raw" (the document as ADT sent it).

tools.name: HandlerDebugBatch
tools.description: [read-only] action 'begin': Starts the debugger batch on the stopped ABAP debuggee, else at the AMDP break. In the debugger batch each call of step, step to line, stack, variables, child variables, stack position or setting a variable at the ABAP debuggee, and of step over, continue or the data preview of a table variable at the AMDP break, is recorded under the next number, starting at 1, and answers with empty content. Answers the state_handle: over Streamable HTTP send it as the state_handle argument of every call of the batch (or in the x-mcp-state-handle header). action 'end': Sends the recorded calls of the stopped debuggee in one envelope on the session the batch started on — the ABAP debuggee's session, or the AMDP session's command session — and ends the debugger batch. Splits SAP's answer into each call's parts and answers the number of recorded calls, of requests sent and of parts received; when sending fails, the parts received differ from the requests sent or the answer fails to split, answers that error, and every number of the batch then answers it. action 'answers' (with number or numbers): Answers the calls of the last executed batch by number: for each number asked, the tool's answer, built from the call's parts of SAP's response when the number is first read and kept for later reads; the numbers asked are processed in parallel. Takes one number or a list of numbers; an unknown number answers as unknown.

action.description: begin starts the debugger batch on the stopped ABAP debuggee or at the AMDP break; end sends the recorded calls and ends it; answers reads the last batch's answers by number, with number or numbers.

number.description: answers: one batch number to read, at least 1.

numbers.description: answers: several batch numbers to read, each at least 1, answered in the order given.

tools.name: HandlerBackgroundRunGet
tools.description: [read-only] Reads one of your background runs by its run_handle: running, or finished with what the run tool answered (the system answer as it is, an error included). A read keeps the run. Runs outside batch mode.

run_handle.description: The run_handle a run started with background=true answered.

tools.name: HandlerBackgroundRunList
tools.description: [read-only] Lists your background runs: run_handle, tool, object, when it started, and running or finished. A run's output is read by its run_handle. Runs outside batch mode.

tools.name: HandlerBackgroundRunDiscard
tools.description: [read-only] Removes the kept answer of one of your finished background runs. Works on a finished run; a started run runs to its end. Runs outside batch mode.

run_handle.description: The run_handle a run started with background=true answered.

tools.name: HandlerLeftoverSessionList
tools.description: [read-only] Lists the SAP sessions of this server's destination an ended server process left open (it was killed before logging them off): handle, role (built or debugger), destination, user, when recorded. Read from the session records alone. Only sessions of ended processes are listed. A server starting while exactly one built session of its destination is left is born on it; with several, all stay listed and untaken. Runs outside batch mode.

tools.name: HandlerLeftoverSessionLogoff
tools.description: [read-only] Logs off a leftover SAP session (any role), releasing every lock it holds; only the logoff is sent, credential-free. Its record is deleted afterwards. Runs outside batch mode.

handle.description: The handle of a leftover session, as the list answers it.

tools.name: HandlerBatch
tools.description: [read-only] action 'begin': Starts batch mode on this server. In batch mode each call of a tool marked recordable is recorded under the next number, starting at 1, and answers with empty content. Answers the state_handle: over Streamable HTTP send it as the state_handle argument of every call of the batch (or in the x-mcp-state-handle header). action 'end': Sends the recorded calls in one envelope with the credentials in force and ends batch mode. Splits SAP's answer into each call's parts and answers the number of recorded calls, of requests sent and of parts received; when sending fails, the parts received differ from the requests sent or the answer fails to split, answers that error, and every number of the batch then answers it. action 'answers' (with number or numbers): Answers the calls of the last executed batch by number: for each number asked, the tool's answer, built from the call's parts of SAP's response when the number is first read and kept for later reads; the numbers asked are processed in parallel. Takes one number or a list of numbers; an unknown number answers as unknown.

action.description: begin: switch into batch mode; end: send the recorded calls and leave batch mode; answers: read the last batch's answers by number (with number or numbers).

number.description: answers only: one batch number to read (an integer of at least 1); give this or numbers, not both.

numbers.description: answers only: several batch numbers to read, answered in the order given; give this or number, not both.
